summary: The main article describes a ruthenium-catalyzed ortho C-H arylation process enabled by visible light at room temperature. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope schemes for arylazines and aryl halides, and mechanistic studies involving radical inhibitors and light/dark experiments.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Ruthenium photocatalysis for meta-alkylation (A) and proposed ortho-arylation (B).
items.description: Compares the previously reported Ru-catalyzed meta-alkylation with the newly proposed ortho-arylation under visible light irradiation.

items.description: Optimization of reaction conditions including catalyst, additives, and solvents for the photoarylation of 2-phenylpyridine.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Photoarylation of 2-arylazines with p-bromoanisole (Anis = 4-BrC6H4).
items.description: Explores the substrate scope of various 2-arylazines in the ruthenium-catalyzed photoarylation reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Photoarylation of 2-arylpyridines with various aryl halides.
items.description: Demonstrates the scope of different aryl bromides and iodides as coupling partners in the photoarylation process.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: (A) Intermolecular competition experiment between aryl halides. (B) Reaction in the presence of radical inhibitors. (C) Detection of free p-cymene. (D) Light on/off experiment. (E) Proposed pathway.
items.description: A comprehensive set of mechanistic studies including competition experiments, radical quenching, and a proposed catalytic cycle.
